title: Interpreting transverse and longitudinal wave graphs

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, contexts, values and planned diagrams are original. The mapped evidence grounds graph interpretation, graph construction and direction demands. Intensity and later-topic demands are excluded.

questions.prompt: Explain the difference between a displacement-distance graph and a displacement-time graph for a progressive wave.
A wave transfers energy to the right. The particles of the medium oscillate left and right. Which description is correct?

options.A: The wave is transverse because the graph may have peaks.
options.B: The wave is transverse because the particles oscillate.
options.C: The wave is longitudinal because particle displacement is parallel to energy transfer.
options.D: The wave is longitudinal because particles move permanently to the right.

questions.prompt: A graph has displacement on the vertical axis and time on the horizontal axis. What does one complete curve show?

options.A: The displacements of many particles at one instant
options.B: The displacement of one chosen position at successive times
options.C: The physical path travelled by one particle through the medium
options.D: The positions of successive compressions along the wave

questions.prompt: On a displacement-distance graph for a longitudinal wave, where is a compression represented?

options.A: Where displacement has its greatest positive value
options.B: Where displacement has its greatest negative value
options.C: Where displacement decreases as distance increases
options.D: Where displacement increases as distance increases

questions.prompt: The planned figure shows a displacement-distance graph at one instant for a transverse wave travelling to the right.

figure.purpose: Assess graph reading and immediate particle motion from a transverse spatial profile.
figure.brief: Original black-and-white line graph of displacement against distance. Use a sinusoidal profile with amplitude 3.0 cm and wavelength 0.80 m. Mark P at an upward equilibrium crossing and Q at the next crest. Include axes and scale but no motion arrows.
figure.alt_text: A transverse displacement-distance graph marks P at an upward crossing and Q at a crest.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: State what the graph represents at this instant.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Determine (i) the amplitude and (ii) the wavelength.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: State the immediate direction of motion of the particle at P and explain your answer.

questions.prompt: The planned figure shows a displacement-distance graph for a longitudinal wave. Positive displacement is to the right.

figure.purpose: Assess translation from a longitudinal displacement graph to compressions, rarefactions and a particle pattern.
figure.brief: Original black-and-white displacement-distance graph showing one sinusoidal wavelength. Mark R at the downward zero crossing, S at the following negative peak, and T at the upward zero crossing. Beneath it provide a row of equally spaced equilibrium dots for annotation. Do not label compression or rarefaction.
figure.alt_text: A longitudinal displacement graph marks two zero crossings and a negative peak above equilibrium particles.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Identify whether R and T represent a compression or a rarefaction.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: State the displacement of the particle at S.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: On the equilibrium-particle row, sketch the particle spacing near R and near T at this instant.

questions.prompt: A sound wave travels to the right through air. The planned figure shows the longitudinal displacement of air particles against distance at one instant.

figure.purpose: Assess a mixed application of prior longitudinal classification and current graph interpretation.
figure.brief: Original black-and-white displacement-distance graph for a right-travelling longitudinal wave. Mark U on a negative-slope section, V at a positive displacement peak, and W on a positive-slope section. Add a separate rightward energy-transfer arrow. Do not draw physical particle arrows or spacing.
figure.alt_text: A longitudinal displacement graph marks negative-slope, peak and positive-slope positions for a right-travelling sound wave.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Classify the wave as transverse or longitudinal and justify the classification using two physical directions.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Identify which of U and W lies at a compression and explain how the graph shows this.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Explain why the curved graph is not the physical path followed by the air particle at V.
